title: STORM
summary: OTYKEN draws on Indigenous musical traditions of Siberia. Listen for drums, jaw harp, string instruments, and throat-singing techniques.

title: Sumer is icumen in
summary: This medieval English round dates to the 1200s. Its overlapping voices celebrate the arrival of summer.

title: Sztoj pa moru (Што й па мору)
summary: Polish singing group Laboratorium Pieśni performs a traditional Belarusian song. Listen for layers of voices telling a story about swans and the sea.

title: Ib Ob Peb, Los Seev Cev
summary: Douachi Yang is a Hmong American singer and songwriter from Saint Paul. Her music connects with Hmong language and community.

title: We're Back
artist: Olivia Foa'i, Sulata Foai-Amiatu, Te Vaka
summary: “We're Back,” from Moana 2, is performed by Olivia Foa'i, Sulata Foai-Amiatu, and Te Vaka. Sung in Gagana Tokelau, the song draws on Polynesian music and the powerful rhythms of wooden log drums. The video was filmed in Aotearoa New Zealand and Hawaiʻi and celebrates Polynesian voyaging and connections across the Pacific. Tokelau is the cultural map marker, not the filming location.

title: Arday Baan Ahayoo
summary: “Arday Baan Ahayoo” means “I am a student.” This Somali children's song from Astaan Ubad celebrates learning and school.

title: LA BATUCADA MAS GRANDE DEL MUNDO
summary: AAINJAA is a Colombian percussion group. Batucada is a fast, energetic samba drumming style with many interlocking rhythms.

title: Afrika Hey
artist: Ndlovu Youth Choir, Sun-El Musician & Kenza
summary: South Africa's Ndlovu Youth Choir performs with producers Sun-El Musician and Kenza, combining choral singing and dance music.

title: Supaman
summary: Supaman is an Apsáalooke (Crow) hip-hop musician from Montana. His performance features dancer Acosia Red Elk.

title: One Day
summary: Koolulam brings people together through group singing. This version of Matisyahu's “One Day” celebrates music as a way to connect.

title: Malagueña
summary: Cuban composer Ernesto Lecuona wrote “Malagueña,” inspired by music from Spain. Listen for dramatic melodic changes in Anat Navarro's performance.

title: Sakura
summary: “Sakura” is a Japanese song about cherry blossoms. Kasumi Watanabe performs on a 25-string koto, a traditional plucked-string instrument.

title: Jalikunda African Drums
summary: Jalikunda shares West African drumming and storytelling traditions. Griots are musicians who help preserve community history through song.

title: Malhari
summary: “Malhari” is a Bollywood song-and-dance performance from the Hindi film Bajirao Mastani. Notice the combination of music, choreography, and storytelling.

title: Aku Mahi
summary: This performance draws on Māori language and musical traditions from Aotearoa New Zealand. Listen for the relationship between voice and rhythm.

title: El Derecho de Vivir en Paz
summary: “The Right to Live in Peace” was written by Chilean musician Víctor Jara. Later artists recorded it to call for peace and justice.

title: WARRA BOOLEE
summary: Sona Takele sings in Afaan Oromoo, an Ethiopian language. “Warra Boolee” blends modern pop with Oromo musical influences.

title: ARE YOU READY
summary: Nive Nielsen is an Inuk singer from Greenland who often plays a small red ukulele. This video was filmed during a very cold winter in Uummannaq.

title: Beautiful Karen (กะเหรี่ยง)
artist: Debary ft Toh Pah Doh, Bee Yang & Sa Kaw
summary: “Beautiful Karen” celebrates Karen communities in Myanmar, Thailand, and beyond. Debary and featured artists combine modern pop with Karen cultural expression.

title: HAKUNA MATATA (JAMBO BWANA)
summary: “Jambo Bwana” is a Kenyan welcome song. Listen for Swahili greetings including “jambo” (hello) and “hakuna matata” (no worries).

title: فرقة تكات- يما ويا يابي - بتوزيع جديد - اغاني عراقية سورية تراثية
summary: Syrian band Takkat performs a modern arrangement of a traditional Arabic song, blending older musical heritage with contemporary sounds.

title: É Proibido Cochilar
summary: “É Proibido Cochilar” means “No Sleeping Allowed.” Mari Campolongo performs this lively Brazilian forró song with an asalato, a handheld percussion instrument.

title: 2017 UCLA PCN Filipino Tinikling
summary: Tinikling is a Filipino folk dance in which dancers time their steps between moving bamboo poles. The poles make a rhythm of their own.

title: Hip-hop tinikling
summary: This performance adds a contemporary hip-hop style to Filipino tinikling. Watch how dancers coordinate with the moving bamboo poles.

title: Lead with Love
summary: Melanie DeMore's “Lead with Love” is about persistence, hope, and supporting one another. Its repeating words invite everyone to sing.

title: ព្រោះតែអូន
summary: Vann Lida performs a cover of a song associated with Cambodian singer Sinn Sisamouth. A cover is a new performance of an existing song.

title: (Awolnation Rework)
summary: MEUTE is a German techno marching band. Its brass and percussion instruments recreate sounds often associated with electronic dance music.

title: Carnaval de mi tierra
summary: Los Hermanos Lovo play chanchona music from El Salvador. Their song celebrates the carnival of San Miguel, with violins and a large string bass.

title: Playing God (Official Music Video)
summary: Polyphia is an instrumental rock band known for intricate guitar playing. “Playing God” combines acoustic-style guitar sounds and modern rhythms.

title: Classical Dragon
summary: Tim Henson and Marcin bring together different guitar-playing techniques. Watch how they make both melodies and rhythms with their instruments.

title: Could You Be Loved
summary: Bob Marley & The Wailers combine reggae and disco influences in “Could You Be Loved,” a song about love and being true to yourself.

title: Get Up Stand Up
summary: Bob Marley's reggae song “Get Up, Stand Up” encourages listeners to speak up for their rights. Listen for the repeated chorus and rhythmic groove.

title: SOUL MAKOSSA
summary: Cameroonian musician Manu Dibango made “Soul Makossa” famous. Makossa is dance music from Cameroon; listen for saxophone, funk, and jazz influences.

title: Con Gái Miền Tây
summary: Vietnamese singer Lương Khánh Vy performs a song connected with the Mekong Delta, a region known for rivers, canals, and boats.

title: G.oka - Ana Msh Faker El Kobleh
summary: Egyptian musician G.oka performs mahraganat, a high-energy electronic street-music style. The playful title means “I don't remember the verse!”

title: Los que se quedan, los que se van
summary: Venezuelan band Desorden Público sings about people who leave their homeland and those who remain. The song expresses sadness and hope for reunion.

title: Yene Habesha (የኔ አበሻ)
summary: Abby Lakew sings in Amharic and celebrates Ethiopian culture. Watch for shoulder movements connected with the Ethiopian dance eskista.

title: Walallay
summary: Afrikaan Ali shares music connected with the Afar people of Ethiopia and nearby countries. Listen for rhythmic clapping and singing.

title: Weni (ወኒ)
summary: Timnit Welday's music connects with Tigrinya-speaking communities of the Horn of Africa. Notice how the singing and dancing fit the beat.

title: Vuelvo
summary: “Vuelvo” means “I return.” Nicaraguan reggae musician Philip Montalbán explores connections to home, family, and Afro-Caribbean culture.

title: Dashain Aayo
artist: Prabin Bajracharya, Praanjal Bajracharya, Ramita Ahdikari
summary: “Dashain Aayo” means “Dashain has arrived!” This song celebrates an important festival in Nepal.

title: Larsha Pekhawar
artist: Ali Zafar ft. Gul Panra & Fortitude Pukhtoon Core
summary: “Larsha Pekhawar” means “Go to Peshawar.” This Pashto-language performance combines singing and rap; listen for the rubab string instrument.

title: Marryuna
summary: Baker Boy is an Aboriginal Australian rapper who performs in Yolŋu Matha and English. “Marryuna” celebrates dance and language.

title: Bugambilia
summary: Colombian group Nasa Histoires blends pop and jazz. The bougainvillea flower in “Bugambilia” represents hope during difficult feelings.

title: Deora
summary: Bangladeshi musician Pritom Hasan blends modern pop with traditional boat-racing song influences. “Deora” celebrates teamwork and energy.

title: Oye Como Va
summary: Playing for Change brings musicians from around the world together for “Oye Cómo Va,” blending Latin rhythms and rock.

title: Koi Ladki Hai
artist: Lata Mangeshkar and Udit Narayan (playback singers)
facts: From the 1997 film Dil To Pagal Hai
The title means ‘There Is a Girl.’
The song playfully connects laughter and singing with monsoon rain.
Playback singers record the vocals heard while actors perform onscreen.
summary: “Koi Ladki Hai” is a Hindi film song from Dil To Pagal Hai. Lata Mangeshkar and Udit Narayan sing while actors perform on screen.

title: Montuno
facts: From the 1993 album Mi Tierra (‘My Homeland’).
Written by Cuban musician Juanito Márquez.
Son montuno uses repeating musical patterns, percussion, and call and response.
The lyrics celebrate music, dancing, and community.
summary: Gloria Estefan's “Montuno” celebrates Cuban son montuno, with repeating instrumental patterns, percussion, and call and response.

title: Dúlaman
summary: “Dúlaman” is a traditional Irish-language song about seaweed. Celtic Woman's arrangement features singer Lisa Lambe.

title: Maskara
summary: Saint Levant and Mohammed Assaf perform Palestinian Arabic pop. The video features dabkeh, a group dance with synchronized steps and stomps.

title: S.O.S.
summary: French singer Indila's “S.O.S.” is about feeling lost and calling out for help. Listen for the emotion in her voice.

title: DRUM TAO
facts: DRUM TAO is a taiko drumming group from Japan.
Wadaiko are Japanese drums of different shapes and sizes.
The group combines drumming, coordinated movement, and dance.
Drums have been used in Japan for centuries at festivals and performances.
summary: DRUM TAO is a Japanese taiko ensemble. Its performers combine powerful wadaiko drums, coordinated rhythms, and movement.

title: Finess
facts: Video link needs correction: spreadsheet currently points to DRUM TAO.
summary: Michael Prince's contemporary performance invites you to notice the connections among rhythm, singing, and movement.

title: Liquindi
facts: Women and girls make rhythms by striking the water surface.
Ostinato means a repeating musical pattern.
Polyphony means multiple different musical lines sounding together.
summary: Liquindi is a Baka water-drumming tradition from Central Africa. Women and girls strike the water to make interlocking rhythms.

title: Desafinado
summary: “Desafinado” means “out of tune.” This bossa nova song playfully answers critics; listen for gentle guitar rhythms and jazz-influenced melody.

title: Love Song
summary: Inuit throat singing often involves two performers exchanging short rhythmic sounds. Listen for breath, repetition, and playful interaction.

title: Dirree
summary: Kemer Yousuf performs in Afaan Oromoo, a language spoken in Ethiopia. Listen for Oromo-language singing and contemporary sounds.

title: Tjovane (the thieves)
summary: Spokanki performs “Tjovane,” a Norwegian story song about thieves, with layered voices, frame drums, and tambourine.

title: Nour El ain
summary: Egyptian singer Amr Diab's “Nour El Ain” means “light of my eyes.” The Arabic pop song blends guitar and dance rhythms.
